crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Citation Graphs Over Time
children.blurb: Citation graphs over time are the record of which research works cite which others, arranged so that the order of publication and the direction of influence are both visible.

children.name: Clustering Papers by Meaning
children.blurb: Clustering papers by meaning groups research works according to what they are about rather than where they were published or who wrote them.

children.name: How a Paper Is Cited
children.blurb: How a paper is cited covers the paths a reference takes from one work to the next: who cites whom, in what context, and how those links accumulate into a citation graph.

children.name: Bridge Studies Between Fields
children.blurb: Bridge studies between fields are research works that connect two or more disciplines by tracing how methods, findings or vocabulary move from one to the other.

children.name: Forecasting Research Trends
children.blurb: Forecasting research trends is the practice of using citation networks, publication records and text signals to estimate which topics, methods or authors are likely to grow or fade in the near term.

sections.body: Citation mapping and discovery is the work of turning the citation links between papers into something a reader can actually navigate. Every paper leaves a trail of references, and software now builds graphs from those trails at a scale no person could trace by hand. In practice this means a reader can open a paper and see what it built on, what came after it, and which other papers sit close to it in meaning. The site's own library of 319 research papers and 14104 extracted claims is the kind of material these tools operate on, since claims give finer resolution than citations alone. The aim is not to rank papers but to show the shape of a research area.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The mechanics are largely solved. Citation graphs can be built, updated and queried reliably, and clustering papers by meaning works well enough to group a field into recognisable neighbourhoods. What is not solved is meaning itself. A citation can be a polite nod, a serious disagreement or a passing mention, and automated systems still struggle to tell these apart without reading the surrounding text. Clustering also drifts, because two papers can look similar in vocabulary while arguing opposite things. Trend forecasting is the weakest area, since research directions bend with funding, fashion and events that no citation record contains. Treat any forecast as a rough sketch, not a prediction.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: The five pages here move from structure to interpretation to speculation. Citation Graphs Over Time covers the raw network and how it grows, which is the place to start if you want to see the underlying data. Clustering Papers by Meaning takes that network and groups it, useful when you want to find a neighbourhood rather than a single paper. How a Paper Is Cited zooms in on one link and asks what kind of link it is, which matters when you are judging whether a citation supports or disputes a claim. Bridge Studies Between Fields looks at the papers that connect otherwise separate clusters, the ones that carry methods across disciplines. Forecasting Research Trends sits at the far end, using the same graph to guess where attention is heading, and it is best read after the other four so you can see how thin the evidence under a forecast really is.
